reasons: Both answers make the same core case: habituation, recovery as the real fix, and tiered protection with type-to-confirm only for boards, and both give full specs. B goes a little further on second-order effects, noting that friction tickets could replace lost-data tickets and that typing DELETE doesn't check whether the selection is right (it suggests typing the count instead), while A names no downstream effect beyond slowing users down. A has a slightly richer edge-case list, but B's extra state (submit with no match), its handling of duplicate board names and its explicit fallback if the PM insists give it a narrow edge.
